cards.headline: Home prices are crashing.
cards.question: In October, what happened to the typical home price in the DC metro compared with a year earlier?
cards.line: Typical DC metro price, down {{dc_price_change}} from a year earlier. Baltimore metro: {{balt_median_price}}, no change.
cards.explain: That's a dip, not a crash. Typical here means the median: half of homes sold for more, half for less.
cards.read: Prices are getting softer at the edges. Bright MLS does not expect big price drops in most markets over the next few months.

cards.headline: Nobody is buying homes.
cards.question: How did new purchase contracts in the DC metro change in October compared with a year earlier?
cards.line: New DC metro contracts in October. Showings fell {{dc_showings_change}}. Across the whole Bright MLS region, {{region_closed_sales}} homes still closed, {{region_closed_change}} fewer than a year earlier.
cards.explain: Fewer buyers is not zero buyers. Homes still sell. Each sale just takes more work.

cards.headline: Mortgage rates are finally dropping.
cards.question: On November 5, how did the average 30-year mortgage rate compare with a year earlier?
cards.line: Average 30-year rate on November 5. A year earlier it was {{rate_year_ago}}.
cards.explain: The headline is half right. Rates have eased for three weeks in a row, but they're still about a point above last year. Your buyers in DC and Maryland pay close to this national average.
cards.math: On a {{dc_median_price}} home with 20% down, that one point adds about {{payment_gap}} a month to principal and interest.

cards.headline: Unemployment is low. Jobs are fine.
cards.question: Which part of our area has unemployment higher than the national rate?

choices.text: DC, Prince George's and Charles counties

cards.line: Unemployment in DC, Prince George's and Charles counties in July. The whole Washington region, Northern Virginia included: {{wash_metro_unemp}} in September. The U.S.: {{us_unemp_sep}} in September.
cards.explain: Where you draw the map changes the story. The region as a whole looks fine. Its inner core is doing worse than the country.
cards.caution: The 5.2% is not seasonally adjusted and comes from a different month, so treat the comparison as rough.

cards.headline: Homes are sitting on the market for months.
cards.question: How long did a typical DC metro home take to sell in October?
cards.line: Typical time to sell in the DC metro, one day slower than a year earlier. Baltimore metro: {{balt_dom}} days, four days slower. Homes for sale across the region: up {{region_listings_change}}.
cards.explain: Typical homes still move in a few weeks. Buyers have more homes to choose from, so the first two or three weeks matter most.
cards.read: The homes that sit for months are usually priced too high for this market.

cards.headline: Home sales are moving onto the blockchain.
cards.question: What has Maryland done about putting property records on a blockchain?
cards.line: Gov. Moore signed SB 168 on May 26, 2026. The state assessments office has to report on using blockchain for property and lease records by {{md_study_due}}.
cards.explain: Deeds are still recorded by each county the usual way. A study is not a switch.
cards.read: Changes at Maryland closings are likely years away.

cards.headline: Crypto finally has clear rules.
cards.question: What happened to the CLARITY Act, the big crypto rulebook, in the Senate?
cards.line: The Senate vote on September 15, 2026. It needed 60 yes votes to move forward. The House passed the bill earlier.
cards.explain: Who polices most crypto is still unsettled. If a buyer wants to use crypto at a DC or Maryland closing, bring in a lender who handles it, early.

takeaways: National headlines don't live on your street. Check the local number before you react.
DC metro prices dipped a little. Contracts and showings fell a lot. Slower, not crashed.
Rates eased from the fall peak but are still about a point above last year.
Where you draw the map changes the jobs story.
Maryland is studying blockchain records, and the big crypto rulebook stalled. Nothing changes at closings yet.
